results.title: how can managers spot people who are working two full- ...
results.content: ## how can managers spot people who are working two full-time jobs at once? Aside from conflict of interest issues (which can be hugely important but which don’t sound like the part you’re worried about), the grounds for an employer to object to someone working multiple full-time jobs is if the person’s performance is suffering because of it, right? Good managers should *always* be doing things like working closely with new hires so they can spot problems and course-correct early on, setting clear goals that represent meaningful progress and monitoring people’s progress against those goals (so it’s easy to see if someone is hitting the bar you need or not), giving feedback, and being direct about problems. There’s always some risk of this when you’re managing people — not just with people working other jobs, but with people citing fictitious personal circumstances to get more grace at work.
